mechanism: This is an evidence variant of the existing character-action typography module carousel. Lock one original clearly adult stylized performer through a stable silhouette, palette and center axis. Rotate at least four high-contrast cards; each card introduces only one original short word and binds it to one readable pose, step, strike, occlusion or reveal. Let geometric backgrounds respond to that same action while preserving identity anchors. End by combining the performer and a new original mark in a still lockup. Do not copy the source performer, words, colors, typography, choreography or timing.

invariants.rule: Lock one clearly adult performer with a stable silhouette, palette and center axis.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing proportions turns each card into a different character.

invariants.rule: Introduce no more than one new original short word per module.
Bind every word to one semantic performer action or occlusion.
invariants.purpose: Makes type and performance share one cause.

invariants.rule: Repeat at least two graphic anchors while geometry changes.
invariants.ablation_failure: Fully unrelated cards feel like a compilation.

invariants.rule: End with performer and original mark together in a held lockup.
invariants.ablation_failure: A moving abstract ending loses the character.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

source rings, speed lines and exact card layouts
